summary: The toy3d aesthetic remains largely consistent with bright lighting and uniform character designs throughout the reel. However, text card positioning obscures facial features during close-ups, and a few standalone prop assets appear overly primitive.

clean: Floating ball hands and limbless character geometry adhere consistently to the style rules.
Shadows, outdoor park lighting, and interior kitchen environments maintain visual continuity.
unclean: Shot 3: Cell 7 retains the yellow character and text from the previous topic rather than introducing the calabaza mate.
Shot 8: The stainless steel mate model resembles an unstyled flat metal can rather than drinkware.

clean: Consistent soft clay materials and vibrant, well-lit environments.
Font styling and lower-third headline cards maintain coherent branding.
unclean: Shot 6: Headline box in cell 14 directly covers the character's eyes and glasses.
Shot 4: Unidentified metallic tool clips into the top edge of cell 9.

issues.problem: Headline graphic covers character eyes and glasses in cell 14.
issues.fix: Shift the headline card upward or adjust camera framing.

issues.problem: Stray metal rod element clips through upper edge in cell 9.
issues.fix: Clear extraneous rig objects outside the visible camera frame.

issues.problem: Steel mate model is a generic grey cylinder.
issues.fix: Add contoured rim and proper mate cup geometry.

issues.problem: Cell 7 visuals misalign with narration introducing the calabaza mate.
issues.fix: Sync shot transition so prop view begins with the audio cue.

learnings.rule: Avoid placing headline text boxes across character eye lines in close-ups.
Model featured prop assets with recognizable silhouettes instead of basic geometric primitives.
